_comment: Reviewed manual attribution entries, for distributions whose wheel metadata
does not supply what Apache-2.0 requires to travel with a redistributed copy.
Each entry states why the automatic reading is insufficient and points at a
licence text checked in under packaging/attribution/notices/.
An override is a claim by the person responsible for the distribution, not a
finding of this tooling. packaging/attribution.py verifies only that the
referenced files exist and that the required fields are filled in; it does
not and cannot confirm that the licence named is the correct one.

pyside6-essentials.reason: The PySide6-Essentials wheel declares 'LGPL-3.0-only OR GPL-2.0-only OR GPL-3.0-only' with no embedded licence file. QICOM relies on the LGPLv3 option and links dynamically; the verbatim LGPLv3 text, the GPLv3 text it incorporates by reference, and QICOM's own statement of how it links are reproduced in the referenced file.

shiboken6.reason: Same wheel family and same missing licence file as PySide6-Essentials; covered by the same reproduced text.

python-gdcm.license: Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause AND IJG AND OFFIS AND MIT AND Zlib AND OpenSSL AND LicenseRef-socketxx
python-gdcm.reason: The python-gdcm wheel ships only the Apache-2.0 licence of its packaging code, not those of GDCM and of the libraries compiled into its binaries (IJG libjpeg with the DCMTK patches, CharLS, OpenJPEG, Expat, zlib, libuuid, md5, socket++; OpenSSL 1.1.1k on Linux, 3.5.2 on macOS). The referenced file reproduces the wheel's Apache-2.0 text and those licences, verbatim from GDCM v3.2.6, the revision python-gdcm 3.2.6 builds, and from OpenSSL_1_1_1k.
